pr_title: Unify the behavior between two way to bind server.
pr_body:
Motivation:

Explain here the context, and why you're making that change.
Unify the behavior between two way to bind server.

Fixes #11013

issue_context.title: localAddress will be null when AbstractBootstrap#bind(SocketAddress localAddress) directly.
issue_context.body:
### Expected behavior
If user use bootstrapServer.bind(PORT) directly, the variable `localAddress` will be null. And if user use bootstrapServer.localAddress(PORT), then execute bootstrapServer.bind(), the variable `localAddress` will not be null.

case one:
```
            ServerBootstrap b = new ServerBootstrap();
            b.localAddress(80).bind();
```

case two:
```
            ServerBootstrap b = new ServerBootstrap();
            b.bind(80);
```

I think what ever user to bind the address, the final result should be same. And when the address is null, the message is also different. I think it also shoube be same.

case one: 
```
            throw new IllegalStateException("localAddress not set");
``` 

case two:
```
            ObjectUtil.checkNotNull(localAddress, "localAddress")
```

review_comments: I think this is not correct... as its not a "builder" method which means it shouldn't change the bootstrap itself. @chrisvest thoughts ?
I agree. The parameter is more like an override of a default. Those who want to know what address was bound in the end, will have to get the address via the ChannelFuture.
Just reserve bind() without param will be more reasonable. But due to history issue, it can't be remove easily.
So I think we should just close this as "won't fix"... @chrisvest agree ?
For the address binding, yes. It still makes sense to have the exceptions unified in master, if they aren't already.
reopen a pr to unify the exception message?
